# MCP server

The WP Waterfall MCP server at https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com lets Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, or another AI assistant look at your sites and change them, always as you and never with more access than you have.

The WP Waterfall MCP server lets an AI assistant look at your WP Waterfall sites and change them. It speaks the Model Context Protocol to the assistant and the public WP Waterfall API to WP Waterfall, holds no data of its own, and acts as the person who approved it, so it can never do more than you can.

## What is the server address?

```
https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com
```

Add it as a remote server (Streamable HTTP) with OAuth sign-in. You need no API key and nothing to install. The **Connections** tab of **Integrations** shows the address with a copy button while no app is connected.

## How do I connect an assistant?

| Client | What to do |
|---|---|
| Claude (web, desktop, and mobile) | Open **Settings**, then **Connectors**, then **Add custom connector**. Name it WP Waterfall and paste the address. Steps: [Claude Desktop](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/claude-desktop). |
| Claude Code | Run `claude mcp add --transport http wpwaterfall https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com`, then run `/mcp` and choose **Authenticate** for wpwaterfall. Steps: [Claude Code](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/claude-code). |
| Cursor | Add `{"mcpServers": {"wpwaterfall": {"url": "https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com"}}}` to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, then choose **Connect** next to wpwaterfall. Steps: [Cursor](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/cursor). |
| ChatGPT | Turn on developer mode in **Settings**, then **Connectors**, then **Advanced**. Create a connector, paste the address, and choose OAuth for sign in. Which plans offer this depends on OpenAI. |
| Any other client | Choose a remote server (Streamable HTTP) with OAuth sign in and paste the address. |

## What does approving do?

The assistant opens a WP Waterfall sign-in page. You sign in, pick the company, and choose **Approve** or **Deny** on one screen, with an **Access** choice of **Full access** (the default) or **Read only**. A read only connection can look at your sites, logs, and settings but cannot change anything: WP Waterfall refuses every tool that changes things, whatever the assistant asks. Full access is everything your role allows, and never more. Staff tools are never available this way. Integrations appears once your company has a plan. The screen, reconnecting, and revoking are in [MCP connections](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp-connections).

## What can the assistant do?

Every tool your role may use, covering sites and environments, code, WordPress, domains and DNS, backups, jobs, access, and billing. A viewer's assistant sees only read tools, and a developer's does not see billing tools. The [MCP tools reference](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/tools) lists every tool, its scope, and its guards.

Tools that change a site return a job. The assistant calls `wait_for_job`, which follows the job for up to 120 seconds and returns the final state. Every tool that looks up a site by name also needs `sites:read`. Site names are unique across all customers, so a taken name answers `site_name_taken`.

The server also offers two prompts. `set_up_local_development` sets up DDEV on your computer with a short lived key: see [Ask your AI assistant to set it up](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/develop-locally-with-ddev#can-my-ai-assistant-set-it-up). `set_up_github_actions` makes a short lived key and a Git token, puts them in GitHub secrets, and adds a workflow that pushes to staging and promotes to live after an approval: see [Deploy from GitHub Actions](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/github-actions).

Anything that deletes, spends money, deploys, rolls back, restores over live, or changes access works in two steps with a yes from you in the chat, and deleting a site or an environment also needs its typed name. The full list of guards is in [Tools and guardrails](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/tools-and-guardrails#what-are-the-guardrails).

## How do I turn on more tools?

The tools sit in toolsets. A new connection gets the everyday sets, and the others (webhooks, files, DNS, security, team, and more) are off to keep the assistant's context small. Ask the assistant to turn one on, for example "enable the webhooks toolset". It calls `list_toolsets` and `enable_toolset`, and the server tells the client its tool list changed.

| Client | What to do |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | Ask in the chat. Claude Code reads the changed tool list at once. To start with a set, add the address with `?toolsets=`: `claude mcp add --transport http wpwaterfall "https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com/?toolsets=sites,webhooks"`. |
| Claude Desktop and Claude on the web | Ask in the chat. If the new tools do not show, edit the connector address to add `?toolsets=webhooks` and reconnect. |
| Cursor | Ask in the chat, or put the address with `?toolsets=` in `mcp.json` and restart the server. |
| ChatGPT | The connector reads its tool list when you create or refresh it. Put `?toolsets=` in the address you paste, for example `https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com/?toolsets=sites,webhooks`. |

`?toolsets=` works in every client, because it decides the list before the client first asks for it. See [Tools and guardrails](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/tools-and-guardrails#how-do-i-load-fewer-tools-or-more) for every set.

## How do I teach the assistant my pipeline?

Download the Claude skills from the card under the server address on the **Connections** tab. They explain how a push, a build, a promote, and a restore work, so the assistant uses the tools in the right order. See [Claude skills for WP Waterfall](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/claude-skills).

## How do I revoke access?

Select **Revoke** on the assistant's row in the **Connections** tab of **Integrations**. The assistant loses access within 5 seconds. See [MCP connections](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp-connections#how-do-i-reconnect-or-revoke).

## Quick answers

**Can the assistant delete a site by accident?** No. You must type the exact site name in the chat. To remove the power altogether, approve the connection with **Read only**.

**Why does the assistant not see a tool?** Your role does not allow it, its toolset is off, or the connection is read only.

Still stuck?

Email support@wpwaterfall.com with your site name and what you tried, or [send us a message](/contact).
